key_insight: Extended strain-induced defects and remanent strain in magnetite do not measurably shift or broaden the Verwey transition, unlike point defects.
engineering_relevance: Plastic deformation can create substantial residual damage without degrading the Verwey transition, so extended slip-related defects are less harmful than point-like disorder for this electronic phase change.
method: Dark-field x-ray microscopy to map defect structures, lattice orientation, and residual strain after unloading
AC magnetic susceptibility to measure the Verwey transition temperature and sharpness
Compare uniaxially compressed samples along [011] and [001], including fractured and non-fractured states
evidence_signal: Across compressed and fractured samples, the measurements show clear remanent structural disorder but no measurable change in transition temperature or transition sharpness.
watch_item: The conclusion is based on macroscopic measurements, so smaller local perturbations near defects may still be present even if they do not affect the bulk transition detectably.
paper_title: Robustness of the Verwey transition against remanent strain-induced defects in magnetite
